name: Bella Dosa
steps: Rinse the rice and chana dal until the water runs mostly clear. Put them in a deep bowl with 350 ml of the measured water and soak for 5–6 hours, until both grains are soft enough to grind. Keep the soaking liquid.

Drain, reserving the liquid. Grind the soaked rice and dal with fresh coconut and cardamom to a smooth batter. Add the reserved liquid gradually so the batter pours from a ladle but is thicker than a thin crepe batter.

Break up the jaggery and dissolve it in the remaining 100 ml measured water over low heat. Strain out grit, cool until just warm, then stir it into the batter. Rest the batter for 10 minutes and check that it still pours in a thick ribbon.

Heat a flat griddle over medium-low heat and rub with a little measured ghee. Pour a small ladle of batter and spread gently to a circle about 12 cm wide. Drizzle a little more ghee around the edge and cook for 2–3 minutes until the underside is golden and the top has set.

Lift the dosa carefully; flip for about 30 seconds only if the top remains damp. Repeat with the remaining batter and ghee, lowering the heat if jaggery darkens too quickly. Serve two warm sweet dosas per person.
tips: Jaggery browns faster than plain dosa batter, so keep the pan at medium-low heat. The coconut is ground into the batter; no sweet filling is required.
passiveTime: Soak the rice and chana dal for 5–6 hours.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
